calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Rangers
calls.body: The Canucks’ penalty kill is the league’s worst, and the Rangers’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Canucks tonight.

calls.title: The Rangers’ power play did its job
calls.plain: The Rangers’ power play created at least its usual chances. The Rangers went 1 for 2 on the power play.
calls.said: the Rangers’ power play would get its usual chances against the Canucks’ shaky kill
calls.beyond: The Rangers have a better power play than most, and Vancouver has one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a big night: the Rangers’ power play created 19.3 expected goals per 60, against their usual 8.5 (about 10.0 against Vancouver) and a league average of 7.8. A team strays this far about once every 70 games.

calls.head: Strength in numbers for the Canucks
calls.body: The Canucks roll four lines, but the Rangers lean on their top six. Vancouver is one of the league’s best for depth, and the Rangers are one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Canucks.

surprises.head: The Rangers picked Vancouver’s defense apart
surprises.body: The Rangers usually get better looks than most teams, and Vancouver usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: the Rangers’ shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.1% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.7% (about 7.1% against Vancouver) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

surprises.head: Vancouver brought the hits
surprises.body: Vancouver’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 163, against their usual 105 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Gawdin scores his first two NHL goals as the Rangers beat the Canucks
paras: Elias Pettersson (#40) got the scoring started for the Canucks midway through the first, with Brock Boeser picking up his 500th NHL point on the goal. Gabe Perreault made it 1-1 for the Rangers late in the period. The second period belonged to the Rangers. Oliver Bjorkstrand gave the Rangers the lead on the power play midway through the period. Glenn Gawdin, in his 15th NHL game, scored his first NHL goal less than five minutes later to make it 3-1. Alexis Lafrenière pushed the lead to 4-1 a little over two minutes later, and Gawdin scored his second NHL goal 56 seconds later to make it 5-1.

The Rangers carried the play, and got the result to match. Dylan Garand made 27 saves for the Rangers, and Leevi Meriläinen stopped 26 of 31 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Adam Fox had the best night of anyone.
The Rangers killed all four Canucks power plays. The Rangers improved to 12-8-1, third in the Metropolitan, while the Canucks fell to 3-17-1, still last in the NHL.
